abstract:
Purpose 
                     The purpose of this paper is to conduct a usability evaluation of governmental data portals and provide a list of best practices for improving stakeholders’ ability to discover, access, and reuse of these online information sources. 
                   
                   
                     Design/methodology/approach 
                     The developed methodology was based on the comprehensive literature review that resulted in a benchmarking framework of the most important criteria. A usability testing method was then applied with accordance to unique requirements of open data portals. This approach was demonstrated by using of a case study. 
                   
                   
                     Findings 
                     The main found weakness was a lack of support for active engagement of stakeholders. The list of best practices was introduced to improve the quality of these portals. This should help to improve the discoverability and facilitate the access to data sets in order to increase their reuse by stakeholders. 
                   
                   
                     Social implications 
                     The creation of appropriate open data portals aims to fulfill the principles of open government, i.e., to promote transparency and openness through the publication of government data, enhance the accountability of public officials and encourage public participation, collaboration, and cooperation of involved stakeholders. 
                   
                   
                     Originality/value 
                     This paper proposed a new approach for the usability evaluation of open data portals on national level from an ordinary citizen’s point of view and provided important insights on improving their quality regarding data discoverability, accessibility, and reusability.

abstract: This White Paper reports the outcome of a Workshop on “Research Data Service Discoverability” held in the island of Santorini (GR) on 21–22 April 2016 and organized in the context of the EU funded Project “RDA-E3”. The Workshop addressed the main technical problems that hamper an efficient and effective discovery of Research Data Services (RDSs) based on appropriate semantic descriptions of their functional and non-functional aspects. In the context of this White Paper, by RDSs are meant those data services that manipulate/transform research datasets for the purpose of gaining insight into complicated issues. In this White Paper, the main concepts involved in the discovery process of RDSs are defined; the RDS discovery process is illustrated; the main technologies that enable the discovery of RDSs are described; and a number of recommendations are formulated for indicating future research directions and making an automatic RDS discovery feasible.

title: “Cataloguers Hub”: a cloud-based platform for cooperative cataloguing and metadata quality assessment
abstract:
Purpose 
                     Numerous sources of organised information are created, published and circulated in every unit of time across the globe. As an administrator of the systematic recording of information sources in a library, the cataloguer’s task becomes hectic and painstaking. Due to various reasons, some libraries opted to outsource professionals for cataloguing, in which quality check or scrutiny of every data field is not possible for the administrator. The libraries invest a lot of time, effort and money in cataloguing similar sources in their collections. The primary purpose of this research is to address quality-control issues, support cataloguers in producing high-quality work and enhance cooperative cataloguing. An automated tool, “Cataloguers Hub”, has been developed during this research in the cloud environment. In this research article, the development of the “Cataloguers Hub”, its features, needs and the scope for future development are described in detail. 
                   
                   
                     Design/methodology/approach 
                     To conduct this research, a mixed-methods approach is used. Through rigorous review of the literature, key problems are identified and objectives are framed accordingly. The assessment framework has been identified and selected as the foundation for conducting the error analysis. Agile methodology was implemented to develop the online platform. 
                   
                   
                     Findings 
                     “Cataloguers Hub” is the prime outcome of this research. It is designed as a dedicated platform for cataloguing, providing services and enhancing cooperative activities in cataloguing. It is a digital hub where cataloguers can register, access the required catalogue records from the database, contribute to the system’s database in standard format and check the quality of the available catalogue. The system can detect and help to reduce duplicate records in the catalogues. 
                   
                   
                     Originality/value 
                     This study fulfilled the need for an online platform to collect, contribute quality metadata and also assess existing catalogue records of libraries. This research can be viewed as a nascent initiative to explore the latent scope of open-ended cooperative cataloguing on a single platform, aiming to save time, effort and cost in cataloguing, while also maintaining and improving the quality of cataloguing practice.

title: Sustainable tourism and environmental impact assessment based on Big Data
abstract: Introduction: Big data enables monitoring of tourism’s environmental impacts through mobility, satellite, and social data. Existing research applies machine learning for prediction and assessment. However, existing research face limitations in data integration, scalability, privacy concerns, and a lack of standardized frameworks for sustainable tourism decision-making. Objective: This research proposed a big data–driven analysis for sustainable tourism and environmental impact assessment using advanced machine learning techniques. Method: The Kaggle platform provides access to a dataset of 9,321 samples on tourism and environmental impact, collected from relevant tourism authorities and environmental agencies. The data involve rigorous preprocessing, including data cleaning with missing value handling, which prevents bias and incomplete records, and Min–Max normalization to scales standardizes, ensuring quality and consistency. Feature extraction is followed by Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) to identify hidden patterns and correlations between tourism intensity and environmental degradation indicators such as land-use change, vegetation density, and resource consumption. The Killer Whale Algorithm-tuned Weighted Random Forest (KWA-Weighted RF) is used in predictive modelling to estimate tourism demand and assess environmental effect trends. KWA optimizes hyperparameters, improving both search efficiency and prediction accuracy. Weighted RF increases robustness by emphasizing critical characteristics and managing imbalance. Results: Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Python-based big data-driven models achieve accuracy (98,7 %), precision (96,3 %), [user2.1][w2.2]recall (95,1 %), F1-score (95,7 %), Kappa (0,964), MAE (0,112), RMSE (0,168), and AUC (0,982) in both tourism demand estimation and environmental impact classification. Conclusion: The findings highlight that sustainable tourism management can be significantly enhanced through data analytics and AI-based decision support systems.
